title: A theoretical and computational analysis of full strong-branching
contribution: Proves that strong branching is near-optimal for vertex cover parameterized by the integrality gap and recursively applies Nemhauser-Trotter persistency, gives an exponential separation where any fractional-only tree loses, and measures four branching rules against DP-computed optimal trees (strong branching within a factor of two on ten classes with up to 20 binaries).
problem_entry: Strong branching is the rule everyone imitates (ML imitation line) but nobody knows how far it is from the smallest possible tree (pp. 3-4).
key_idea: Parameterized analysis on vertex cover plus an exact 3^O(n) dynamic program over faces of the cube to report every rule as a ratio to the optimal tree (pp. 5-6, 11, 21-22).
assumptions: Binary MILP, worst-bound node selection with depth tie-break, product score with eps=0 for theory; Assumption 1 (solver finds an integral optimal LP solution if one exists) makes the optimal tree well defined; adversarial most-fractional LP solver for Theorem 3 (pp. 5-6, 9, 11).
proof_devices: depth counting with half-integrality gain of 1/2 per strong-branching child (Lemma 1, Theorem 1, pp. 14-15)
disjoint-triangles tight instance and match with bounded-search-tree FPT bound (Remark 1, p. 6)
Nemhauser-Trotter persistency plus Picard-Queyranne union lemma for a maximal integer set inherited by children (Prop. 1, Thm 2, Lemma 3, pp. 6-8, 15-16)
diamonds-plus-triangles gadget under an adversarial LP solver, binomial-sum lower bound (Thm 3, pp. 9, 17-18)
Bodur-Dash-Gunluk extended formulation applied to the cross-polytope for a fractional-only vs integer branching separation (Prop. 2, Cor. 1, pp. 9-10, 19)
face DP recurrence OPT(F)=1+min_j(OPT(F_j0)+OPT(F_j1)) with cascading 0-nodes and grouped parallelism (Thm 4, Alg. 1, pp. 11, 21-22)
experiments: Ten random classes x 100 instances with <=20 binaries (packing, covering, lot-sizing variants, vertex cover, two CCPs, bipartite stable set + knapsack); SB-L, SB-P, most infeasible, random vs DP-optimal tree; geometric-mean ratios, performance profiles, per-instance tables, % integer branchings in optimal tree; own hypothesis rejected; word of caution on extrapolation; LP solver and B&B code not named in the text (pp. 11-13, 22-29, 36-45).
positioning: Against intricate greedy variable rules and ML imitation of strong branching; first upper bound depending on a specific variable rule, first explicit fractional-vs-integer branching separation (pp. 2-3, 8-10).
writing: Main results section before proofs; provably good / provably bad / computational bullets; scare-quoted 'optimal' with footnote; aggregate claim 'always performs the best' stronger than per-instance tables (pp. 4-5, 12, 44).
limits_future: Only up to 20 binaries, may not extrapolate; room for better rules (CCP portfolio); suggests learning from optimal trees (pp. 12-13, 29).

method_links.note: Strong branching as an unexplained solver practice; absolute-quality question; parameterized instance model because worst case is exponential.
DP-optimal trees as ground truth up to 20 binaries, ratio reporting, word of caution.
Tight instance (Remark 1) and FPT match; positive class paired with exponential negative class; cost of the extended formulation noted.

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Fixes an LP solver returning the most fractional optimal vertex to separate strong branching from a natural greedy rule by 2^Omega(n).

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: structural statistic of the optimum as explanatory variable
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Tabulates % integer-variable branchings in the optimal tree next to rule ratios and tests (and rejects) a hypothesis with it.

transferable: Exact exponential DP over the 3^n faces of the cube as ground truth for branching rules on <=20 binaries, with cascading pruning and coordinate-group parallelism (pp. 21-22).
Make an implementation-dependent measure well defined by a numbered solver assumption plus a short observation (pp. 10-11, 20).
Prove an FPT-type bound for a solver rule on vertex cover and match it with a tight instance and the known FPT algorithm (pp. 5-6).
Lift an instance to an extended formulation to show a branching restriction is exponentially costly (p. 19).
coauthors: Yatharth Dubey, Marco Molinaro, Prachi Shah

quotes.text: However, to the best of our knowledge there is no understanding of how good strong-branching is in absolute terms.
A common way to meaningfully analyze an algorithm with exponential worst-case performance is to show its performance with respect to some parameter

title: Decomposable formulation of transmission constraints for decentralized power systems optimization
contribution: Proves that external-zone injection shift factors pass through boundary-bus shift factors, yielding an equivalent block-diagonal ISF formulation with few linking constraints and an N-1 scheme without contingency copies, and shows on SCUC instances up to 6,515 buses that decentralized ADMM finds solutions within 0.13% of the central optimum where the phase-angle formulation fails.
problem_entry: Decentralized market clearing needs a DC power-flow formulation that is both local (phase-angle) and scalable with N-1 (ISF); each incumbent has only one of the two (pp. 1-3).
key_idea: Theorem 1: ISF columns of far-zone buses are weight-sum-one combinations of boundary-bus columns, so most ISF coefficients can be dropped with boundary variables; external outages handled by lagged constants turned into robust per-line bounds (pp. 9-14).
assumptions: DC linearization; connected zones without islands; zero injection at boundary buses (made non-restrictive by artificial buses); two zones; outages create no islands; ADMM with binaries is a heuristic; lagged external-outage scheme has no guarantee (pp. 2, 4-5, 12, 14-16).
proof_devices: zone partition of the reduced Laplacian with zero off-diagonal blocks (pp. 9-10)
Claim 1: move the injection to boundary buses by changing only far-zone angles, solvable since Q is non-singular (pp. 9-10)
flow preservation gives weights summing to one; nonnegativity stated but not argued in the proof read (pp. 9-10)
redundancy of contingency balance equations via sum-one weights (Prop. 1, p. 13)
8-bus numerical example before the theorem (Example 1, p. 8)
experiments: SCUC on 7 MATPOWER European cases (1,888-6,515 buses), 2 zones from an auxiliary MILP, Julia/JuMP + CPLEX 12.9 on one desktop with MPI, 1 h limit; baseline decentralized phase-angle with same ADMM and relaxed barrier tolerance; metrics time, residual, iterations, gap to central optimum; proposed avg 600 s, 0.13% gap, phase-angle no feasible solution; N-1 avg 1170 s, 0.08%; single run per instance (pp. 15-20).
positioning: Extends ADMM power-systems work and revises Feizollahi et al.'s release-and-fix; corrects Biskas-Bakirtzis (internal contingencies only); ties sparsity to Dey's sparse-cut papers; criticizes thresholding of small ISF entries (pp. 3-4, 6, 16).
writing: Structural fact stated at end of introduction; one theorem plus constructive sections; generality hedged as 'we stress' applicability to any DC power-flow problem (pp. 3-4, 19).
limits_future: Only SCUC tested; optimal zone subdivision open; unstated: two-zone tests only, no guarantee for lagged outage scheme, no dual bound (p. 19).

method_links.note: Deliverable is a heuristic decentralized primal solution measured by gap to the central optimum, not a certificate from a relaxation; Dey is third author on an Argonne-led paper.
Ground truth is the centrally computed optimum, but compared inside a full solver setting, not a stripped instrument.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: exact structure-exposing reformulation of network physics
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Proves an identity of the DC power-flow ISF matrix that turns a dense formulation into an equivalent block-diagonal one for decomposition (also S059's CVXNLP equivalence).

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: lagged coupling constants as robust bounds
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Freezes cross-zone terms at the previous ADMM iterate so all external-outage constraints collapse into one robust bound per line.

transferable: Partition the reduced Laplacian by zones and use zero off-diagonal blocks to show far-zone effects pass only through boundary buses (pp. 9-10).
Replace contingency copies by per-line robust bounds built from lagged coupling constants (p. 14).
Split benchmark networks into zones with a small MILP minimizing boundary buses under a balance tolerance, documented in an appendix (p. 20).
Measure a decentralized heuristic by its gap to the centrally solved optimum on benchmarks (p. 17).
coauthors: Álinson S. Xavier, Feng Qiu (Argonne National Laboratory)

quotes.text: The formulation is based on the fact, which we prove in Section 3, that the injection shift factors of external zones are a convex combination of the shift factors at boundary buses.
In comparison, the decentralized phase-angle formulation failed to solve even the smallest test cases, even when allowed very relaxed convergence and feasibility tolerances.

title: A reformulation-enumeration MINLP algorithm for gas network design
contribution: Proposes a binary-search-on-budget framework whose probes combine a convex CVXNLP-based master with diameter and configuration binaries, a nonconvex nomination-validation subproblem and no-good cuts, plus a cost-only IP for lower bounds, and solves design-from-scratch instances on GasLib networks up to 582 nodes (feasible budgets for all 25 GasLib-582 instances, 12 optimal).
problem_entry: Design-from-scratch gas network MINLP with discrete diameters, active elements and non-tree networks has never been solved beyond about 500 nodes (pp. 1-2, 4).
key_idea: Use the convex energy program CVXNLP, whose KKT system equals the network analysis equations, as master of a combinatorial decomposition and check only the remaining potential bounds and active-element constraints in a subproblem; binary search on budget outside (pp. 9-15).
assumptions: Steady-state potential-loss law, strictly increasing loss function with phi(0)=0 for Theorem 1, compressor and valve models from prior work, four diameter choices per pipe, no operating cost (pp. 2, 5-9, 11, 16).
proof_devices: KKT equivalence between CVXNLP and the network analysis equations with potentials as flow-conservation multipliers (Thm 1, Appendix A, pp. 11, 27-28)
exclusion of simultaneous q+ and q- by strict monotonicity (p. 27)
explicit max{0,.} construction of bound multipliers for the converse (p. 28)
SOC representation of q^3 <= t (eq. 62, pp. 16-17)
validity of lower bounds from the no-good-cut IP argued in prose (pp. 13, 15)
experiments: GasLib-11/24/40/134/582 (4197 dropped as too hard), nominations x stress 0.1-2.0; three master implementations tried (BARON/SCIP cubic, MOSEK SOCP, Gurobi quadratic+perspective), Gurobi chosen; BARON on the direct MINLP as baseline, Gurobi dropped for constraint violations; adapted Borraz-Sanchez MISOC gave no feasible solution; gap, time, time-to-20%-gap, iteration counts; BARON wins at high stress on small nets; GasLib-582 all feasible, 12 optimal, 6 under 20%; perspective avg 55% max 97% gap improvement; no infeasible budget ever proved (pp. 15-26).
positioning: Builds on CVXNLP (Cherry, Collins et al., Raghunathan) and Babonneau-Nesterov-Vial; contrasts with Borraz-Sanchez et al. MISOC and tree-network methods; prior work characterized by instance size (pp. 4, 9-10, 18).
writing: Hedged first-at-scale claim; plain reporting of where BARON wins; minor inconsistencies (cold 4218 vs 4128; stress list printed with 0 instead of 0.1) (pp. 2, 16, 19, 26).
limits_future: GasLib-4197 too hard; large gaps at high stress and cold nominations; cannot prove infeasible budgets; lower bound on GasLib-582 relies on BARON; future: operating cost (pp. 15, 19, 23-24, 27).

method_links.note: Convex program used to generate primal designs, not as a relaxation for dual bounds; lower bounds from a cost-only IP with no-good cuts and from BARON.
Solver returning violated solutions dropped; limit stated that the framework never proves an infeasible budget.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: exact structure-exposing reformulation of network physics
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Replaces nonconvex network analysis equations by the convex CVXNLP via KKT equivalence and uses it as a decomposition master (also S047's ISF identity).
Reports time to reach 20% optimality gap for unclosed instances, echoing the 20% gap-closed rule of thumb in the skill.

transferable: Binary search on budget where each probe is a convex master + nonconvex validation + no-good cut loop updating both bounds (Alg. 1, p. 14).
Cost-only integer program plus no-good cuts as lower-bounding warm start (pp. 13-15).
Implement the same convex master in native nonlinear, SOCP and quadratic+perspective forms and keep the fastest, reporting the losers (pp. 16-17).
Run a global solver for a fixed time for its lower bound and combine it with your framework's upper bound (p. 19).
Report time-to-20%-gap next to final gap (p. 18).

quotes.text: We also discovered that Gurobi at times returns solutions with large constraint violations for this MINLP formulation.
In addition, for all instances, we are not able to prove infeasible budget from the primal bound loop.
